newsitem.title: INDIA: ABN AMRO to arrange $800 mln loan for IOC.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to arrange $800 mln loan for IOC.

text.p: ABN AMRO Bank N.V. said it received a mandate from Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) to arrange a short-term facility for financing oil imports upto $800 million.
"IOC has mandated ABN AMRO Bank N.V. as coordinating arranger to arrange a short-term facility for financing oil imports," it said in a statement on Friday.
"This facility seeks to consolidate its core short-term funding requirements for oil import financing and curtail its frequent tapping of the short-term market," it added.

The facility is underwritten for $400 million (with a $100 million greenshoe option) and has a tenor of 12 months, which would enable IOC to tie in funding for at least $800 million, and upto $1.0 billion on oversubscription, ABN AMRO said.
It said each financing is typically for six months.
State-run IOC has a monopoly of crude oil imports and imports the bulk of India's petroleum product requirements.
"IOC is a well-known and highly regarded borrower in the international markets and has frequently tapped the market for short-term funding to finance oil imports," the bank said.
ABN AMRO said it was the first time a pricing grid linked to the long-term sovereign foreign currency debt rating has been incorporated in a facility for an Indian borrower.
"This is consistent with the perception of IOC as a strong credit constrained by the sovereign rate ceiling," it said.
The other arrangers of the loan are Kredietbank N.V. and Dresdner Southeast Asia Ltd.
